slot.brief: Four orderings of electron gain enthalpy across groups/periods (with Cl vs F anomaly, noble gases); identify which order is wrong — higher-order trend analysis.

stem: Each sequence is intended to run from less negative to more negative electron gain enthalpy. Which sequence is incorrectly ordered?

verdicts.working: Electron gain enthalpies (kJ mol⁻¹) are approximately I −295, Br −325, F −328, and Cl −349. Thus the order from less negative to more negative is I < Br < F < Cl, not the order in (D).

working:
Halogens, from less negative to more negative electron gain enthalpy: $\text{I}<\text{Br}<\text{F}<\text{Cl}$. Since Cl has a more negative value than F, option D is misordered. Ar has positive electron gain enthalpy; the other sequences follow the known trends.

Independent check: Electron gain enthalpies (kJ mol⁻¹) are approximately I −295, Br −325, F −328, and Cl −349. Thus the order from less negative to more negative is I < Br < F < Cl, not the order in (D).
solution:
For halogens, electron gain enthalpy becomes more negative in the order $\text{I}<\text{Br}<\text{F}<\text{Cl}$; chlorine is more negative than fluorine.
Hence $\text{I}<\text{Br}<\text{Cl}<\text{F}$ is incorrectly ordered.
